data.title: Product Engineer
data.description:
Experience: 3. 00 + years

Salary: INR 4500000-6000000 / year (based on experience)

Expected Notice Period: 15 Days

Shift: (GMT+05: 30) Asia/Kolkata (IST)

Opportunity Type: Office ()

Placement Type: Full Time Permanent position(Payroll and Compliance to be managed by: Astra)

(*Note: This is a requirement for one of Uplers' client - Astra)

What do you need for this opportunity?

Must have skills required: 

LLM, Typescript/React, Node Js, Node/react, Websockets, AI Agents, Tool calling

Astra is Looking for: 

Supa Health is building the agentic operating system that makes this work disappear - an AI scribe, an AI receptionist, and an agentic back office that handles benefits verification, prior auth, intake, and claims. Every call its agents make, every denial they work, every payer quirk they encounter feeds back into a system that gets sharper the next time. We''re building software that compounds. 

We''re not selling dashboards. We''re replacing the work itself. 

Small team, $5M from Peak XV (formerly Sequoia India), shipping fast. Looking for our founding product engineer. 

What You''ll Work On

The honest answer is: whatever moves the product furthest. We have surface area in every direction and we''d rather you pick the one that fits you than wedge you into a slot. 

That could mean: 

Operator-facing surfaces. Real-time, dense, information-rich SPAs where our back-office team works through hundreds of cases a day. The interaction model matters as much as the engineering - operators live in these tools eight hours a day, and small wins compound into hours saved. Modern React stack, TypeScript end-to-end, real-time over WebSockets. 

The agent platform. The systems that let our agents do real work in the world - making calls, navigating systems built before APIs existed, parsing structured and unstructured payer responses, and writing back into our own state. Worklfows for orchestration, Postgres as the source of truth, LLMs invoked deliberately rather than reflexively. 

The platform underneath both. Schema, services, auth, multi-tenancy, integrations, and the HIPAA-grade segregation that has to be right on day one. Postgres, Drizzle, Fastify, an Nx monorepo, WorkOS for auth. 

The next product wedge. We have a roadmap. We also have customers asking for things that aren''t on it. Founding engineers at Supa Health get to argue for what we should build next, and then build it. 

You''ll talk to operators. You''ll talk to clinic owners. You''ll watch someone do their job for two hours and then go automate the painful parts of it. You''ll ship something on Tuesday and see it running in production on Wednesday. 

What We Look For

Craft. You''ve shipped real software to real users for years and it shows in how you think. You have opinions about schema design, about when to reach for a state machine, about what makes a UI feel fast. You can tell the difference between extra effort and meaningful quality, and you reach for the second one. Your code reviews make the people around you better - not because you''re harsh, but because you''re specific, and the team''s standards rise around you. 

Judgment. Healthcare is full of edge cases that look like bugs and bugs that look like edge cases. The CTO can''t be in every decision and we don''t want to use process as a substitute for thinking. We want people who can reason through a tradeoff with incomplete information and make the call. 

Ownership. You don''t wait for work to be handed to you. You see what''s broken, what''s slow, what''s missing - and you write the doc, file the issue, or open the PR. You take a problem from "I noticed this" to "it''s deployed and working, " which means talking to the user, designing the solution, writing the code, watching it land, and going back to fix what you got wrong. 

Direction. You work with users and teammates to figure out what to build and how to build it. You sit with operators, watch where they get stuck, and come back with a sharper definition of the problem than we started with. You''re a thought partner to the team - not someone waiting for a spec, and not someone going off to build in a vacuum. 

Speed. Not crashed-out hustle-culture speed. The kind of speed that comes from deleting unnecessary work, making decisions quickly, and not being precious about being wrong. 

Range. You don''t need to be a 10/10 at frontend, backend, infra, AI, and product. You do need to be willing to learn whichever of those the work demands this week. 

Must Have: 

3+ years building production software. We care less about the years and more about the slope - what you''ve shipped, what you learned the hard way, and what you''d do differently now. You''ve lived in TypeScript and Postgres long enough to have real opinions about both. 

Good to Have: 

Agentic AI / LLM systems. You''ve built something with agents, tools, evals, and the unglamorous plumbing around them. You know when an LLM is the right answer and when it''s a fancy way to make a slow, wrong API call. 

Early-stage startup experience. You know what it feels like to have no design system, no playbook, no PM, and a customer call in 90 minutes. 

Healthcare / RCM background. You know what a 271 is. You''ve fought with a clearinghouse. You have feelings about Availity. This is rare and we''d love to find it, but we''ll happily teach the right person. 

How We Hire

We borrowed our process from Linear because we think they got it right. 

Intro call with the CTO. ~30 minutes. We talk about you, the company, and whether the role fits. We''ll discuss comp on this call. 

Technical conversation. ~60 minutes. We work through a real problem together. No leetcode. 

Paid work trial. 2-5 days, paid at our standard daily rate. You work on something real. You meet the team. You leave with a much clearer picture of whether Supa Health is the right place for you, and we leave with a much clearer picture of whether you''re the right person for Supa Health. 

Decision. Independent feedback from the trial team, then a debrief, then an offer (or honest feedback if not). 

Who This Isn''t For

We''d rather be honest now than waste your time later. 

If you need a roadmap handed to you, you''ll be uncomfortable here. The roadmap is a conversation, and you''re in it. 

If you want a 9-to-5, that''s a legitimate and healthy choice, and it isn''t this job. We don''t expect crunch, but we expect founding-team intensity. 

If you''d rather not talk to users. Operators and clinic owners are part of your job, not someone else''s. 

Interview Process: 

L1- Introduction with the CTO

L2- Technical Conversation

L3- Paid Work Trial

L4- Decision

How to apply for this opportunity?

- Step 1: Click On Apply! And Register or Login on our portal. 
 - Step 2: Complete the Screening Form & Upload updated Resume
 - Step 3: Increase your chances to get shortlisted & meet the client for the Interview!

About Uplers: 

Our goal is to make hiring reliable, simple, and fast. Our role will be to help all our talents find and apply for relevant contractual onsite opportunities and progress in their career. We will support any grievances or challenges you may face during the engagement. 

(Note: There are many more opportunities apart from this on the portal. Depending on the assessments you clear, you can apply for them as well). 

So, if you are ready for a new challenge, a great work environment, and an opportunity to take your career to the next level, don't hesitate to apply today. We are waiting for you!

data.description:
About This Role

In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a Tamil Quality Assurance Lead (QAL) to oversee quality, consistency, and trainer performance across Tamil AI training projects. You will review AI-generated Tamil content and trainer/QA work, evaluate output quality against project guidelines, provide precise written feedback, and ensure that all contributors follow the expected quality standards. 

You will assess work for accuracy, fluency, grammar, spelling, tone, cultural appropriateness, meaning preservation, instruction-following, formatting, and adherence to project-specific rubrics. You will spot recurring quality issues, communicate updates to trainers and QAs, support onboarding, maintain documentation, and help activate contributors who are not working consistently. This role requires strong Tamil and English skills, excellent attention to detail, structured communication, and the ability to manage quality workflows across remote teams. 

This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world's largest AI companies and foundation-model labs. Your Tamil quality leadership will directly help improve the world's premier AI models by ensuring that Tamil training data is natural, accurate, culturally appropriate, well-documented, and aligned with client expectations. 

Selection process involves an AI interview, a domain-specific task, and an interview with a recruiter. 

Your profile

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Tamil, Linguistics, Translation, Communications, Journalism, English, Education, Quality Assurance, or a relevant domain/related field. 
 - Native or near-native Tamil proficiency with strong reading and writing skills. 
 - Strong grasp of the English language to follow project guidelines, communicate with teams, and provide clear feedback in English. 
 - 3+ years of professional experience in Tamil writing, editing, translation, localization, content QA, AI training, education, annotation, or related language-review workflows. 
 - Strong understanding of Tamil grammar, spelling conventions, punctuation, tone, register, regional variation, and cultural context. 
 - Ability to evaluate Tamil content against detailed rubrics and identify issues such as mistranslation, literal phrasing, unnatural tone, hallucinated claims, ambiguity, or inconsistent terminology. 
 - Experience leading or supporting remote teams of trainers, annotators, reviewers, editors, or QAs is strongly preferred. 
 - Comfortable working in fast-moving remote environments using tools such as Discord, Google Sheets, Google Docs, trackers, dashboards, and project management systems. 
 - Highly detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to maintain style guides, FAQs, trackers, onboarding materials, honeypots, and other quality documentation. 
 - Experience with AI training, data annotation, large language models, prompt/response evaluation, or rubric-based LLM QA is a strong plus. 

Key responsibilities

- Quality monitoring: Spot-check Tamil items, identify quality issues, provide ongoing feedback through DMs, and escalate recurring or critical issues. 
 - Trainer and QA communication: Update trainers and QAs on Discord about new item guidelines, project changes, workflow updates, and quality expectations. 
 - Question handling: Respond to trainer/QA questions clearly and promptly, especially around Tamil wording, register, translation fidelity, cultural context, regional variation, and edge cases. 
 - Trainer/QA activation management: DM contributors who are inactive or not working, encourage activation, track follow-ups, and flag availability issues when needed. 
 - Documentation: Create and maintain Tamil project documentation, including style guides, trackers, FAQs, quality notes, examples, honeypots, and onboarding materials. 
 - Onboarding and training: Schedule and run onboarding/training calls with trainers and QAs to explain project expectations, workflows, rubrics, quality standards, and Tamil-specific style requirements. 
 - Quality alignment: Ensure all trainers and QAs apply Tamil language guidelines consistently and understand updates as projects evolve. 
 - Process improvement: Identify recurring quality gaps, propose workflow improvements, and help build scalable QA processes for Tamil-language projects.

data.title: Malayalam Linguistic QA Specialist (Remote)
data.description:
About This Role

In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a Malayalam Quality Assurance Lead (QAL) to oversee quality, consistency, and trainer performance across Malayalam AI training projects. You will review AI-generated Malayalam content and trainer/QA work, evaluate output quality against project guidelines, provide precise written feedback, and ensure that all contributors follow the expected quality standards. 

You will assess work for accuracy, fluency, grammar, spelling, tone, cultural appropriateness, meaning preservation, instruction-following, formatting, and adherence to project-specific rubrics. You will spot recurring quality issues, communicate updates to trainers and QAs, support onboarding, maintain documentation, and help activate contributors who are not working consistently. This role requires strong Malayalam and English skills, excellent attention to detail, structured communication, and the ability to manage quality workflows across remote teams. 

This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world's largest AI companies and foundation-model labs. Your Malayalam quality leadership will directly help improve the world's premier AI models by ensuring that Malayalam training data is natural, accurate, culturally appropriate, well-documented, and aligned with client expectations. 

Selection process involves an AI interview, a domain-specific task, and an interview with a recruiter. 

Your profile

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Malayalam, Linguistics, Translation, Communications, Journalism, English, Education, Quality Assurance, or a relevant domain/related field. 
 - Native or near-native Malayalam proficiency with strong reading and writing skills. 
 - Strong grasp of the English language to follow project guidelines, communicate with teams, and provide clear feedback in English. 
 - 3+ years of professional experience in Malayalam writing, editing, translation, localization, content QA, AI training, education, annotation, or related language-review workflows. 
 - Strong understanding of Malayalam grammar, spelling conventions, punctuation, tone, register, regional variation, and cultural context. 
 - Ability to evaluate Malayalam content against detailed rubrics and identify issues such as mistranslation, literal phrasing, unnatural tone, hallucinated claims, ambiguity, or inconsistent terminology. 
 - Experience leading or supporting remote teams of trainers, annotators, reviewers, editors, or QAs is strongly preferred. 
 - Comfortable working in fast-moving remote environments using tools such as Discord, Google Sheets, Google Docs, trackers, dashboards, and project management systems. 
 - Highly detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to maintain style guides, FAQs, trackers, onboarding materials, honeypots, and other quality documentation. 
 - Experience with AI training, data annotation, large language models, prompt/response evaluation, or rubric-based LLM QA is a strong plus. 

Key responsibilities

- Quality monitoring: Spot-check Malayalam items, identify quality issues, provide ongoing feedback through DMs, and escalate recurring or critical issues. 
 - Trainer and QA communication: Update trainers and QAs on Discord about new item guidelines, project changes, workflow updates, and quality expectations. 
 - Question handling: Respond to trainer/QA questions clearly and promptly, especially around Malayalam wording, register, translation fidelity, cultural context, Kerala usage, diaspora usage, and edge cases. 
 - Trainer/QA activation management: DM contributors who are inactive or not working, encourage activation, track follow-ups, and flag availability issues when needed. 
 - Documentation: Create and maintain Malayalam project documentation, including style guides, trackers, FAQs, quality notes, examples, honeypots, and onboarding materials. 
 - Onboarding and training: Schedule and run onboarding/training calls with trainers and QAs to explain project expectations, workflows, rubrics, quality standards, and Malayalam-specific style requirements.

data.title: HR Systems Assurance Specialist
data.description:
HR Systems Assurance SpecialistSAP Payroll and SuccessFactorsChennai | India

We are seeking an HR Systems Assurance Specialist to provide independent assurance that HR data, payroll and time are accurate, compliant and appropriately controlled across SAP ECC Payroll and SuccessFactors. The role involves independently extracting and reconciling data across systems, investigating discrepancies, testing controls and clearly reporting findings. This is an assurance and reporting role; it does not involve building or configuring the systems. 

Key Responsibilities

Perform recurring data quality checks across SuccessFactors Employee Central and SAP ECC Payroll to assess completeness, accuracy, validity and consistency of HR master data. 

Reconcile payroll results across periods, including headcount, gross pay, deductions, general ledger (GL) and bank postings, and check compliance with statutory and company policy requirements. 

Verify that SuccessFactors Time Tracking data aligns with rosters and time rules and flows correctly into SAP ECC Payroll wage types. 

Monitor Employee Central to ECC replication and investigate errors, missing records and data mismatches. 

Design, perform and document control tests, maintaining clear, audit-ready evidence and supporting audit trails. 

Log findings, follow up with control and process owners on remediation, and report recurring issues and trends. 

Explain findings and potential impacts clearly to HR Technology, payroll teams and HR business stakeholders. 

Key Competencies & Skills

Strong hands-on reporting skills in SAP ECC HCM/Payroll and SuccessFactors, including Story reports and Table reports. 

Good understanding of SAP HCM and SuccessFactors data models, including Employee Central, Time Tracking and the payroll cluster. 

Working knowledge of payroll processes, including gross-to-net calculations, retroactive and off-cycle payroll, and payroll reconciliation. 

Understanding of time management processes, including rosters, overtime, shift and night allowances, public holidays and absence accruals. 

Advanced Excel skills, including Power Query, PivotTables and XLOOKUP; working knowledge of SQL. 

Ability to use Power BI for reporting is preferred; Python or similar scripting experience for automating checks is an advantage. 

Understanding of control design and testing, maker-checker controls, segregation of duties, audit trails and data privacy. 

Strong analytical thinking, professional scepticism, clear written communication and accurate documentation. 

TECHNICAL KNOWLEDGE

SAP ECC HCM / Payroll

Knowledge of key info types: 0000/0001, 0007, 0008, 0014/0015, 2001/2002 and 2010. 

Understanding of payroll cluster PCL2, including RT, CRT and WPBP, and how retroactive calculations appear. 

Experience with or understanding of Wage Type Reporter (PC00_M99_CWTR), payroll journal, PC_PAYRESULT, Ad Hoc Query, SQVI and SE16N. 

Ability to read a payroll schema or PCR and explain a result; configuration or development is not required. 

SuccessFactors Employee Central

Understanding of corporate, succession and country-specific data models, MDF objects, picklists and effective-dated records. 

Experience creating or using Story reports (People Analytics) and Table reports. 

Ability to use the Data Replication Monitor to investigate Employee Central to ECC replication issues. 

SuccessFactors Time Tracking

Understanding of time profiles, time types, time recording profiles, work schedules and holiday calendars. 

Knowledge of time valuation and time collectors, including how approved timesheets flow into ECC Payroll wage types. 

Payroll, Data and Assurance

Understanding of gross-to-net payroll, retroactive and off-cycle runs, and statutory deductions. 

Ability to reconcile headcount, gross pay, GL postings and bank postings period on period. 

Ability to assess roster patterns such as 4x4, 7x7, 14x14 and FIFO, including overtime, shift and night allowances, public holidays and absence accruals. 

Understanding of data quality dimensions: completeness, accuracy, validity, timeliness and consistency. 

Knowledge of GDPR and India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and the importance of protecting employee data. 

Experience & Education Requirements

6-10 years of total professional experience, including at least 4 years of hands-on experience with SAP HCM/Payroll and SuccessFactors data. 

Experience working with multicultural, multi-country teams. 

A degree in Commerce, Information Technology, Engineering or a related discipline. 

Payroll and Time Management experience is an advantage. 

Strong written and verbal English communication skills, with the ability to explain findings to payroll and HR managers without unnecessary technical jargon. 

Self-motivated, analytical and process-oriented, with a collaborative approach to issue resolution and documentation. 

Additional / Preferred Skills

SAP certifications in SuccessFactors Employee Central, SuccessFactors Time Tracking or SAP HCM Payroll. 

Exposure to Employee Central Payroll. 

Interest or experience in automated or AI-assisted assurance checks. 

PRACTICAL SCREENING EXERCISE

As part of the selection process, candidates may be given an anonymised Employee Central extract, timesheet extract and payroll wage-type extract. In approximately 45 minutes, candidates will be asked to: 

Identify employees with approved time but no matching wage type in payroll. 

Identify Employee Central pay changes that have not replicated to ECC. 

Flag overtime that exceeds roster rules. 

Name the control that could have prevented each issue. 

LOCATION & WORKING HOURS

Location: Chennai, India. 

Flexible working hours to overlap with operating sites in the Americas, Africa and Australia. India Standard Time is approximately 8. 5-10. 5 hours ahead of the Americas, depending on location and daylight-saving time. 

Who We Are

Glencore is one of the world's largest global diversified natural resource companies and a major producer and marketer of more than 60 commodities. Through a network of assets, customers and suppliers that spans the globe, we produce, process, recycle, source, market and distribute the commodities that advance everyday life.

Automation Development & Framework Ownership

Non-Functional Testing

- Contribute to performance, reliability, and resilience testing

Observability & Debuggability

- Leverage logs, metrics, and traces to improve test reliability

Test Data & Environment Management

- Design and manage test data strategies and datasets

Incident & Operational Support

- Assist in troubleshooting defects across environments

Technical Skills

 - Exposure to: 
 - Cloud platforms (Azure preferred)

 - Experience using AI-assisted tools responsibly (e. g. , GitHub Copilot)
Key Expectations

data.title: Director-Software Engineering-Unify Energy
data.description:
We are seeking an experienced and strategic Director of Software Engineering to lead engineering for the Unify Energy platform. This role will provide technical, organizational, and delivery leadership for software and data capabilities serving the oil and gas industry. The Director will align engineering execution with customer and business priorities while advancing a secure, scalable platform that helps energy organizations manage high-value information, streamline operational workflows, and improve access to trusted data across the asset lifecycle. 

The Director will partner closely with Product Management, business leadership, Architecture, Information Security, DevOps, Data Engineering, Quality Engineering, Implementation, Customer Success, and other software teams. This leader will translate industry needs into an executable engineering strategy, coordinate cross-team dependencies, and ensure that product investments produce measurable customer, operational, and financial outcomes. 

The ideal candidate is a hands-on strategic leader with deep experience delivering complex SaaS and cloud-native platforms, leading distributed engineering teams, and building data-intensive solutions for regulated or asset-intensive industries. Oil and gas domain experience is strongly preferred, including familiarity with upstream, midstream, or downstream workflows; land, lease, well, facility, and asset records; regulatory information; document and data onboarding; and integration with industry and enterprise systems. 

Roles And Responsibilities

- Lead, mentor, and develop high-performing engineering teams responsible for the Unify Energy platform and related software, data, integration, and automation capabilities. 
 - Own the engineering strategy, technical roadmap, execution plan, and delivery outcomes for Unify Energy in alignment with product strategy, customer commitments, revenue goals, and long-term platform direction. 
 - Build strong working partnerships with oil and gas business leaders, customers, Product Management, Implementation, and Customer Success to understand industry workflows, prioritize the highest-value problems, and convert business outcomes into clear engineering plans. 
 - Provide technical leadership across SaaS software engineering, cloud-native architecture, APIs and integrations, data pipelines, search and document services, analytics, workflow automation, and applied AI. 
 - Oversee the full software development lifecycle, from discovery and architecture through development, testing, deployment, monitoring, support, and continuous improvement. 
 - Drive delivery of scalable, secure, and maintainable capabilities that support energy information ingestion, normalization, indexing, classification, validation, search, retrieval, workflow, and reporting. 
 - Advance platform capabilities that enable Access to serve as a trusted steward of customers' physical and digital information assets by supporting metadata management, intuitive search, filtering, navigation, and map-based discovery within the SaaS platform. Lead the data engineering capabilities required to ingest, organize, and enrich customer data so it becomes more accessible, useful, and valuable across oil and gas workflows. 
 - Guide integration strategy for industry and enterprise systems, including data exchanges, APIs, batch interfaces, identity services, content repositories, GIS or spatial data, analytics platforms, and customer-specific systems of record. 
 - Lead data engineering and data quality practices for high-volume structured and unstructured information, including ETL/ELT, metadata management, lineage, reconciliation, observability, and reliable downstream consumption. 
 - Guide responsible use of AI and machine learning to improve document understanding, metadata extraction, classification, entity matching, search relevance, workflow recommendations, quality assurance, and operational efficiency. 
 - Ensure solutions are designed with appropriate attention to cybersecurity, privacy, records retention, legal hold, auditability, data residency, regulatory obligations, customer controls, and business continuity. 
 - Establish outcome-based planning and measurement. Define engineering and business KPIs for major initiatives, including delivery predictability, quality, reliability, adoption, customer value, operational efficiency, and revenue or retention impact. 
 - Partner with Architecture, Information Security, DevOps, Quality Engineering, Data Engineering, and Operations to establish technical standards, reusable patterns, release controls, service-level objectives, and operational readiness. 
 - Monitor portfolio health, delivery metrics, product quality, reliability, risks, dependencies, capacity, and technical debt; make clear tradeoffs and proactively resolve or escalate issues that threaten business outcomes. 
 - Continuously improve platform architecture, technical health, and integration patterns while protecting customer continuity and sequencing change based on value, risk, and delivery readiness. 
 - Support talent planning through hiring, coaching, performance management, succession planning, role clarity, and the creation of an accountable, inclusive, and customer-focused engineering culture. 
 - Represent Unify Energy engineering in executive, product, customer, and governance forums, providing clear updates on strategy, delivery performance, investment needs, risks, opportunities, and decisions required. 
 - Stay current with emerging trends in energy technology, information management, cloud engineering, cybersecurity, data platforms, AI-enabled automation, SaaS architecture, and software delivery practices. 

First 6-12 Months

The initial focus will be to establish a clear engineering and product delivery baseline for Unify Energy, strengthen alignment between customer needs and the technical roadmap, and improve execution predictability. The Director will assess the platform architecture, team capabilities, operating model, delivery commitments, reliability, security posture, technical debt, and customer integration landscape. They will work closely with Product, Operations, and customer-facing teams to confirm the highest-priority business and product outcomes and translate them into a focused, sequenced delivery plan. 

Success will be demonstrated through clearer accountability, stronger engineering and product operating rhythms, improved delivery and quality metrics, reduced execution risk, deeper customer partnership, and measurable progress on the highest-value Unify Energy capabilities.

Working at Atlassian

Atlassians can choose where they work - whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. We're looking for a Senior Principal Backend Software Engineer to join our team, passionately focused on delivering creative improvements for our engineering teams. 

Your Future Org

"Jira Platform enables Jira to become the trusted, agent-native system of record and control plane for human and agent teamwork at enterprise scale. "

As a Senior Principal Engineer In This Future Organization, You Will Help Turn This Vision Into Reality. Your future team

Jira Data Management focuses on empowering users with effective control over the transfer and management of data within Jira Cloud. For enterprise customers, the capability to move and manage large volumes of data both within and outside their cloud site is essential for leveraging Atlassian's cloud offerings. We develop and support various data migration pathways for Jira products, facilitating transitions from Data Center to Cloud, Cloud to Cloud, and External to Cloud data migrations. The JDM team comprises over 50 engineers, along with product managers and designers, dedicated to overcoming challenges that may hinder customers from fully utilizing our cloud offerings. Each feature we release has a direct impact on Atlassian's cloud revenue. 

We are actively focused on improving reliability at scale, performance, and features for diverse product use cases built on our services. Our mission is high-profile, and we expect our team members to take initiative in driving and contributing to Atlassian's overarching objectives.

data.title: Manager, Construction Quality
data.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all. 

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. 

Job Summary

The Construction Quality Manager is responsible for developing, implementing, and managing the overall Quality Management System (QMS) for large-scale construction projects, ensuring compliance with project specifications, engineering standards, statutory regulations, client requirements, and international quality practices. The role oversees quality assurance and quality control activities across all phases of construction including civil, structural, architectural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), process utilities, cleanroom systems, and high-tech industrial facility installations. The position plays a critical role in ensuring defect-free execution, minimizing rework, maintaining construction excellence, and achieving project delivery targets with the highest quality standards. 

Key Roles & Responsibilities

- Develop, implement, and maintain project-wide Construction Quality Management Plans, Inspection & Test Plans (ITPs), quality procedures, and inspection protocols. 
 - Lead all QA/QC activities for civil, structural steel, architectural, mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, piping, HVAC, cleanroom, and utility systems construction works. 
 - Ensure construction activities comply with approved drawings, project specifications, applicable codes, standards, client requirements, and statutory regulations. 
 - Establish and monitor quality assurance systems for contractors, subcontractors, vendors, and suppliers across the project lifecycle. 
 - Conduct quality audits, surveillance inspections, site walkthroughs, and compliance reviews to identify gaps and enforce corrective actions. 
 - Review and approve Method Statements, Material Submittals, Inspection Requests, Test Reports, Welding Procedures, and quality documentation. 
 - Manage Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), Site Observation Reports (SOR), Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA), Root Cause Analysis (RCA), and quality improvement initiatives. 
 - Coordinate with Engineering, Construction, Procurement, Safety, Commissioning, and Project Controls teams to ensure integrated project execution with required quality. 
 - Oversee testing and inspection activities including concrete testing, welding inspections, NDT, pressure testing, cleanroom validation, and equipment installation quality checks. 
 - Ensure compliance with ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems and applicable international construction standards such as ASTM, ASME, ANSI, NFPA, IPC, SEMI, ACI, AWS, NFPA, FM Global, NEC, IS, DISH, PESO, ATEX, CE, UL and IEC standards. 
 - Shall be developing and implementing Test Protocols for Piping and HVAC in coordination with commissioning team for MEP and other services. 
 - Sustainability shall be conversion with the sustainability and green building requirement. 
 - Monitor contractor quality performance metrics, workmanship standards, punch points, and closure of quality observations. 
 - Lead quality meetings with clients, consultants, EPC contractors, and stakeholders to review project quality performance and risk mitigation actions. 
 - Ensure proper maintenance of quality records, inspection reports, turnover dossiers, as-built documentation, and handover packages. 
 - Support commissioning and startup teams by ensuring all systems are installed and tested in accordance with approved quality standards. 
 - Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance construction quality, reduce defects, improve productivity, and optimize project delivery efficiency. 
 - Mentor QA/QC engineers, inspectors, and site quality personnel while fostering a strong culture of quality excellence across the organization. 

Education & Qualifications Required

- Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Construction Management, or related engineering discipline. 
 - Master's Degree or MBA in Project Management / Construction Management is preferred.

data.title: ASIC Digital Design, Staff Engineer
data.description:
We Are

Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow. 

You Are

You have built verification environments that catch bugs before they become customer issues. Whether you have been doing this for three years or closer to ten, you have learned that verification is not about running tests; it is about thinking through what could go wrong and building the infrastructure to prove it won't. You understand that a well-written testbench is half the battle, and the remaining is knowing which corner cases matter, and which ones are just noise. 

You are comfortable working in System Verilog and UVM, writing test cases that exercise real scenarios, not just the ones in the specification. You have debugged enough simulations to recognize patterns in waveforms, and you know when to dig deeper versus when to loop in the design team. Protocols like MIPI UFS/UniPro, DDR, PCIe, Ethernet or USB are not just acronyms to you; you have worked with at least one of them closely enough to understand how transactions flow and where things typically break. 

Working on a verification team means asking questions when the test plan does not make sense, writing assertions that catch issues, and tracking coverage in a way that tells you what you have validated and what you have not. At Synopsys, you will work on IP cores that go into AI systems, automotive platforms, and data centers. The verification work you do will determine whether that IP works when it ships. 

What You'll Be Doing

- Build and maintain UVM-based testbench for RTL IP cores, including agents, drivers, monitors, scoreboards, and coverage collectors
 - Write System Verilog test cases and constrained random stimulus to verify functional correctness across different operating modes and protocol scenarios
 - Develop and execute verification plans based on design specifications, identifying test scenarios, corner cases, and coverage goals
 - Debug RTL and testbench issues by analyzing simulation logs, waveforms, and coverage reports to isolate root causes and verify fixes
 - Implement assertion-based checks and functional coverage models to track verification progress and ensure thorough validation
 - Collaborate with design engineers to understand IP functionality, clarify requirements, and provide feedback on design-for-verification considerations
 - Run regressions, analyze results, and work toward coverage closure, documenting verification status and outstanding issues

The Impact You Will Have

- Ensure Synopsys IP cores are thoroughly validated before they reach customers building AI accelerators, automotive systems, and cloud infrastructure
 - Reduce post-silicon bugs and customer escalations by catching design issues early through systematic verification and coverage analysis
 - Contribute to faster IP release cycles by building reusable verification components and efficient test strategies
 - Help maintain high-quality standards across Synopsys IP products, directly impacting customer success and product reliability
 - Support the development of verification best practices and methodologies within the Bangalore team
 - Enable design teams to iterate faster by providing clear, actionable feedback on functional correctness and edge case behavior
 - Build verification infrastructure that can scale across multiple IP variants and protocol configurations

What You'll Need

- 4-8 years of hands-on experience in ASIC or RTL verification for IP cores or digital designs
 - Understanding of verification planning, test case development, and coverage-driven verification concepts
 - Working knowledge of UVM or similar verification methodologies, with experience building testbench components and writing test cases
 - Solid System Verilog skills, including understanding of constrained random verification, coverage, and assertions
 - Familiarity with at least one industry-standard protocol such as MIPI UFS/UniPro, DDR, PCIe, Ethernet, USB or similar
 - Experience debugging RTL simulations using waveform viewers and analyzing coverage reports to guide verification progress
 - Experience with Perforce or similar revision control environment
 - Basic scripting ability in Python, Perl, TCL, or shell scripting to support automation and regression management
 - Ability to use AI tools like Cursor and GitHub Copilot for analysis, development, debugs and maximizing productivity. 
 - Have good communication skills, will be a team player, and will have good problem-solving skills. 

Who You Are

- You can look at a design spec and start listing the test scenarios that need to be covered without waiting for someone to hand you a complete test plan

data.description:
Company Overview: 

Flowserve is a global manufacturer of pumps, valves, seals, and aftermarket services, delivering comprehensive flow control solutions that support essential industries such as energy, clean water, and pharmaceuticals. If you're looking for a culture built on ingenuity, innovation, and excellence, Flowserve offers the opportunity to put your experience in motion. Whether you're an individual contributor or a people leader, you'll find meaningful opportunities for professional growth, competitive rewards, and a workplace grounded in our core values: People, Safety, Integrity, Ownership and Ingenuity. At Flowserve, we're inspired by what we can achieve together-creating extraordinary flow control solutions that strengthen today's world while building tomorrow. 

Job Summary

The Nuclear Project QC Engineer is responsible for preparation of ITP referring to applicable ASME codes, customer specification. Ensuring that pumps supplied for nuclear projects meet all applicable quality, regulatory, customer, and project requirements. The role supports inspection, documentation, verification, traceability, and nonconformance control throughout the project lifecycle, from order entry through final shipment. 

The position requires close coordination with Engineering, Quality Assurance, Procurement, Manufacturing, Project Management, and Customers to ensure compliance with contractual and technical requirements throughout the project lifecycle. 

Key Responsibilities

- Review contract, customer, code, and project quality requirements for nuclear pump orders. 
 - Develop inspection and test plans (ITPs) for nuclear projects for pumps. 
 - Interpret customer quality requirements and ensure they are fully incorporated into ITPs, quality plans, and inspection documentation. 
 - Support receiving inspection, in-process, final, and witness inspections as required. 
 - Verify material traceability, certification, and product identification. 
 - Review and approve quality records, MDRs / data books, and turnover packages. 
 - Ensure compliance with applicable nuclear quality standards and project specifications and maintain necessary documents as per ITP. 
 - Interface with engineering, manufacturing, suppliers, customers, and third-party inspectors. 
 - Manage nonconformance reports, corrective actions, and concession / deviation processes. 
 - Support vendor surveillance and sub-supplier quality control activities. 
 - Confirm calibration status of gauges, tools, and test equipment used on the project. 
 - Monitor weld, machining, assembly, testing, and preservation activities where applicable. 
 - Ensure documentation is complete, accurate, and ready for customer / regulatory review. 

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or Diploma in Mechanical Engineering. 
 - 3-7 years of experience in Quality, Inspection, or ITP preparation, preferably in pump manufacturing or rotating equipment industry. 
 - Experience in ASME Sec III is preferred. 

Required Skills & Experience

- Strong knowledge of API 610 pumps, pump components, and auxiliary systems. 
 - Strong knowledge of ASME Sec III. 
 - Good understanding of inspection and testing requirements for castings, forgings, machined parts, fabricated parts, and assembled pumps. 
 - Experience in preparation of ITPs, quality plans, inspection procedures. 
 - Experience in inspection, handling customer witness and customer audits. 
 - Knowledge of customer specifications, project quality requirements, and document review processes. 
 - Familiarity with material certification requirements such as EN 10204 3. 1 & 3. 2
 - Knowledge of NDE methods such as VT, PT, MT, UT, and RT. 
 - Good understanding of welding, heat treatment, hydro testing, performance testing, and final inspection requirements. 
 - Working knowledge of applicable codes and standards such as API 610, ASME Sections V, VIII, IX, ASTM, and other relevant international standards. 
 - Exposure to supplier quality requirements and procurement quality flow-down.

data.title: Staff Digital Verification Engineer
data.description:
We Are

Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow. 

You Are

You have spent years building verification environments that have to catch the bugs no one else saw coming, the corner cases that only show up when three protocols collide and a timing edge goes the wrong way. You know that a test plan is only as good as the bugs it finds, and you have learned to think like the design, like the system integrator, and like the customer all at once. 

You are the engineer who sees a coverage hole at 95% and knows exactly which scenario is missing. Writing assertions is not a checkbox exercise for you, it is how you encode your understanding of what should never happen. You have debugged enough waveforms to know when something smells wrong three layers deeper than the symptom. 

Leading a verification effort means more than running regressions. You set the strategy, you review the test plans your team writes, and you make the call on what gets verified to what depth. You work directly with RTL designers and architects, not to rubber-stamp their work but to push back when the intent is unclear or the interface is going to be painful to verify. 

At Synopsys, you will work on DesignWare IP that ships into real products. The verification environments you build will be used across product generations, and the bugs you catch will never make it to silicon. 

What You'll Be Doing

- Build and evolve SystemVerilog/UVM verification environments for DesignWare synthesizable IP cores, ensuring they scale across multiple product generations and configurations
 - Define comprehensive test plans that cover corner cases, protocol compliance, and system-level interactions for serial interface protocols and memory controllers, including DDR and LPDDR where applicable
 - Write and debug complex testbenches, checkers, and assertions that catch real bugs in critical PHY blocks and interface logic
 - Develop software requirements for the PHY that scale across various configurations and use cases
 - Own verification closure for multiple critical blocks within DDR PHYs, including functional coverage, code coverage, and formal signoff
 - Collaborate directly with RTL designers, digital architects, and circuit teams to align verification scope with design intent and surface issues early in the design cycle
 - Manage regression infrastructure and work with the infra team to optimize verification cycles, debug failures, and keep the environment reliable

The Impact You Will Have

- Your verification environments will catch critical bugs before tapeout, directly affecting the quality and time-to-market of DesignWare IP used across the semiconductor industry
 - The test plans you define and review will set the verification standard for the team, ensuring consistent coverage and reducing escapes
 - Your coverage-driven approach will surface gaps that others miss, leading to more robust IP and fewer silicon respins
 - The assertions and checkers you write will become reusable verification IP, accelerating future projects and raising the quality bar
 - Your collaboration with RTL and architecture teams will shape design decisions early, making designs easier to verify and more reliable in the field
 - The regression strategies you implement will directly improve team productivity and reduce verification cycle time
 - Your ownership of critical PHY blocks will ensure that high-stakes features meet functional and performance requirements on schedule

What You'll Need

- Bachelor's or Master's in Electrical Engineering or Electronics and Communication Engineering with 4+ years of hands-on verification experience
 - Proven track record leading verification teams through IP project delivery, including planning, execution, and signoff
 - Strong experience developing SystemVerilog/UVM testbenches from scratch and evolving them as designs grow in complexity
 - Deep expertise writing test plans, implementing checkers, and building assertions that catch real bugs, not just toggle coverage
 - Proficiency extracting and interpreting functional coverage and code coverage metrics, and using those insights to drive verification closure
 - Experience verifying serial interface protocols and working through IP design and verification processes, knowledge of DDR or LPDDR protocols is a strong plus
 - Demonstrated ability to own end-to-end verification deliverables, including metric closure and formal review signoff, experience with AI-assisted verification tools is a plus

Who You Are

- You can walk into a coverage review, spot the gap in the test plan, and articulate exactly what scenario is missing and why it matters
 - You write assertions that encode real design intent, not just the obvious cases, and you know the difference between a checker that catches bugs and one that just makes noise
 - You are comfortable leading technical discussions with RTL designers and architects, pushing back when verification scope is unclear or the interface is going to create downstream pain
 - You manage multiple verification efforts in parallel without losing track of what is at risk, what is on schedule, and what needs attention today
 - You debug with purpose, you do not just stare at waveforms hoping for insight, you form hypotheses, test them, and move systematically toward root cause
 - You treat verification infrastructure as a product, you care about regression efficiency, debug turnaround time, and whether your environment is actually usable by the rest of the team

The Team You'll Be Part Of

Your recruiter will share more about the team structure and mission during the interview process. 

Rewards and Benefits

We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

data.title: Head of Injection Moulding (Mobile Industry)
data.description:
HEAD OF INJECTION MOULDING

Faridabad, Delhi NCR | On-site | 12-18 years | Reports to the founders Qualification: B. E. / B. Tech or Diploma - Plastics, Polymer, Mechanical or Production Engineering Mobile handset industry moulding experience is mandatory - please read below before applying

Moulding is where our product starts, and where our cost is set. A part moulded badly becomes a part printed badly, assembled badly and rejected at pack - by which point we've paid for all of it. 

You'd own moulding as a function: the floor, the process, the people, the capacity and the capital. That includes overmoulding - rigid shell with soft-touch elastomer - which is a meaningful part of what we produce and a materially harder process than single-shot. 

We are only considering candidates from the mobile handset industry

We want to be direct about this so nobody wastes their time. 

We make small, cosmetically critical parts - sub-millimetre wall sections, visible surfaces with no tolerance for sink or flow marks, tight fit against a device, and cosmetic standards closer to consumer electronics than to general plastics. A part that would pass in most moulding shops gets rejected here. 

The discipline that produces that output is learned in the handset supply chain, and it doesn't transfer quickly from elsewhere. Excellent moulding experience in automotive, appliance, packaging, housewares or general engineering plastics is genuinely excellent experience - it just isn't what this role needs, and we'd be setting you up to struggle. 

So: you should have spent meaningful time moulding handset housings, covers or cosmetic enclosures - at Oppo, Vivo, Xiaomi, Realme, Transsion, Foxconn, Dixon, Lava or in their tier-one supplier base. Adjacent consumer electronics enclosure work at the same cosmetic standard will also be considered. 

The thing that actually limits this floor

We're high-mix. Many moulds, frequent changes, moderate volume per run. In that environment the constraint usually isn't cycle time - it's changeover and the scrap that follows it. Every tool change costs setup hours, then costs more shots before the process stabilises. Across a week of changes that's a serious share of capacity spent producing nothing. 

Most moulding operations measure cycle time obsessively and changeover barely at all. We'd like someone who goes after it. 

What you'd build

- Changeover discipline - SMED method, prepared tooling, parallel setup, and a measured changeover time that comes down
 - Validated parameter sets per mould, so a setter isn't rediscovering the process each time, and a first-off routine that reaches stable quickly and records what stable looked like
 - Material handling discipline - polymer dried to spec before it goes near a machine. Wet resin causes splay and cosmetic defects that get blamed on printing two stations later
 - A skill matrix for setters and operators, with certification before anyone runs unsupervised, and cross-training so capacity doesn't depend on one person's attendance
 - Real downtime and scrap data coded by cause, so improvement has something to aim at
 - Capacity planning and the case for new machines as we grow

You'd own

- Moulding production across shifts, against the plan
 - Scrap and first-pass yield at the machine. Your primary number
 - Process capability, parameter control and changeover performance
 - Machine utilisation, uptime and maintenance coordination
 - Tool condition in production - shot counts, preventive maintenance schedules, spare inserts and components, and escalation to the tool room before a tool fails rather than after
 - Tool repair and refurbishment decisions, with the cost case
 - Moulding capacity decisions and capital proposals
 - The moulding team - setters, operators, helpers, supervisors - including hiring and training
 - Safety, 5S and housekeeping

You need

- 12+ years in injection moulding, with function or plant-level ownership rather than shift supervision alone
 - Mobile handset moulding experience - mandatory. Housings, covers or cosmetic enclosures, at a handset OEM or in their tier-one supplier base. See the note above
 - Hands-on process capability. You can set a machine, read a short shot, and tell a setter what to change and why
 - Defect diagnosis: short shot, flash, sink, weld lines, warpage, splay, burn marks - cause, not just name
 - Material knowledge - PC, ABS, PC/ABS, TPU, PP and filled grades; drying requirements, moisture sensitivity, masterbatch and regrind Overmoulding. A real part of our production and not a side skill: 
 - Two-shot and insert moulding - rotary platen, index and core-back methods, or mould-and-transfer. The machine and tool requirements of each, and when one suits better than the other
 - Material pairing and bond - which combinations bond chemically, which need mechanical interlock, and how melt temperature, shore hardness and surface condition affect adhesion. TPU and TPE over PC and PC/ABS specifically
 - Bond strength as an invisible defect. An overmoulded part can look perfect and delaminate weeks later in a customer's hand. It has to be designed and processed right, because inspection won't catch it. Peel and bond testing is part of the job, not an afterthought
 - Differential shrinkage and warpage between the two materials, and first-shot dimensional stability before the second shot
 - Cycle balancing - the slower shot sets the cycle, which makes process optimisation here a different problem from single-shot
 - Interface flash, colour bleed and the cosmetic defects specific to two-material parts

Tooling, in detail. This is not a nice-to-have for us: 

- Tool construction - mould base and insert construction, steel grades and hardness, cold and hot runner systems, gate types and vestige, cooling layout and what it does to cycle and warpage, venting, ejection, slides and lifters, shut-off surfaces, surface finish and texture
 - Two-shot tool construction - rotation and indexing, sealing at the material interface, second-shot shut-offs, and why these tools fail differently from single-shot ones
 - Tool condition on the floor - reading flash as parting line wear, galling on slides, blocked vents causing burns, scaled water lines quietly adding seconds to cycle, ejector wear, hot runner tip and heater faults. Catching these before they become a stoppage or a scrap run
 - Trials and correction - T0/T1/T2, reading trial results, steel-safe versus steel-removal corrections, shrinkage adjustment, and knowing when a correction is worth doing
 - Repair, refurbish or replace, with the judgement and the cost case behind each
 - The arbitration. The most valuable thing you'll do is decide whether a defect is a tool problem or a process problem. Process people blame the tool, tool rooms blame the process, and the part keeps failing while they argue. We want someone who settles it with evidence
 - Demonstrated changeover or scrap reduction with numbers. We'll ask for before and after
 - Team building across shifts, including developing setters
 - Fluent Hindi; working English

Good to have: tool room or tool design background earlier in your career, scientific moulding or DOE training, multi-cavity and high-cavitation tooling, IMD/IML, take-out robots and automation, SMED implementation, CIPET background, OEE systems. 

Where this sits alongside our Tooling Engineer: they own mould design review and new tool development; you own tools in production - condition, maintenance, correction and when to retire them. You'll disagree occasionally, and that's healthy. 

Tell us: which handset programmes or customers you moulded for, your overmoulding experience and the material pairs you've run, your average changeover time and what you did to it, your scrap rate and how it was measured, one defect where you proved it was the tool and not the process (or the reverse) and how you proved it, and the cosmetic standard you worked to.

Reliability Modeling & Prediction

System-Level Reliability Analysis

data.description:
Experience - 3-5 years

Location - Vikhroli, Mumbai

CTC - 15-18 LPA

About the Role

We're looking for a Frontend Engineer to build and own product surfaces in NymbleUp's web app - the workforce-scheduling, LMS and video-analytics platform used daily by store managers and HR teams at large enterprise clients. You'll work in a Next. js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript codebase (App Router, MUI 7, Zustand, SCSS Modules) of roughly 250k lines, shipping features like the Workforce Scheduler: a virtualized week/day planner that stays interactive with 2, 000+ employee rosters, drag-and-drop shift editing, bulk actions and approval flows. This is a hands-on role for someone who cares about performance, state design and correctness in data-heavy UIs, not just pixel-pushing. 

What You'll Do

- Build and maintain features end-to-end in Next. js (App Router) and React 19 with TypeScript - route, view, store, service layer. 
 - Design client state with Zustand stores and selectors so that single edits don't re-render whole grids; keep server data flows clean through our Axios service layer and typed endpoint modules. 
 - Ship performance-sensitive UI: row virtualization, memoized cells, debounced filters, Web Workers for heavy rollups, and measured frame budgets on large rosters. 
 - Implement complex interactions - drag/resize/copy of shifts, keyboard editing, bulk apply, approval and publish flows - with correct date/time and timezone handling. 
 - Work with the Django backend team on API contracts: read responses critically, log blockers with concrete recommendations, never invent endpoints. 
 - Build with the shared component library and design tokens (MUI theme + SCSS tokens); extend it rather than re-rolling components. 
 - Debug production issues across multi-tenant deployments (auth/token refresh, tenant base-URL resolution, CSP, caching) and trace root causes. 
 - Take part in code reviews, keep typecheck/lint/build green, write clear PR descriptions, and help raise test coverage in a codebase that currently has none. 

Must-Have Qualifications

- B. E. /B. Tech in Computer Science (or equivalent CS engineering degree) - required. 
 - 3-5 years of professional frontend development, with at least 2 years in React + TypeScript on a production product. 
 - Strong React fundamentals: rendering model, memoization, hooks discipline, Server vs Client Components, and why a component re-renders. 
 - Hands-on Next. js App Router experience (layouts, route groups, server components, API/route handlers, middleware). 
 - Solid TypeScript - strict mode, generics, typed API layers, no `any` by habit. 
 - State management at scale (Zustand, Redux or similar) and data-fetching patterns with Axios/fetch, interceptors and token refresh. 
 - Comfort with CSS architecture: SCSS Modules, design tokens, responsive layouts, and a component library such as MUI. 
 - Strong debugging skills - browser DevTools, React Profiler, network traces; able to isolate and fix issues in a large codebase you didn't write. 
 - Strong analytical and logical reasoning - handles date/time, timezone and scheduling edge cases correctly and can defend design decisions. 

Good to Have

- Performance work on large lists/grids: @tanstack/react-virtual, Web Workers, canvas or similar. 
 - Drag-and-drop UIs (@hello-pangea/dnd, react-dnd), rich-text editors (TipTap), charts (Recharts), or data grids (AG Grid). 
 - Experience with multi-tenant SaaS, auth flows (JWT refresh rotation, OTP), CSP/security headers, and frontend VAPT fixes. 
 - Exposure to BFF/route-handler work in Next. js: third-party integrations (Zoho Desk, Google Maps/Sheets), rate limiting, streaming AI chat with the Vercel AI SDK. 
 - Testing: React Testing Library, Playwright or Vitest; helping set up a test culture from scratch. 
 - Node. js deployment basics (pm2, Cloudflare/OpenNext, CDN cache invalidation) and Git-based review workflows with conventional commits. 

What We're Looking For (Mindset)

- A problem-solver who treats a flaky drag interaction or a 5-hour timezone drift as a puzzle, not a chore. 
 - Someone who reads existing patterns before inventing new ones, and asks why before how. 
 - Strong ownership - sees features through from design proposal to verified production behaviour. 
 - A clear communicator who can explain technical trade-offs to backend, product and design peers. 

To apply, share your resume along with a brief note on a performance or state-management problem you solved in a React app and how you approached it.

data.title: Head of Printing
data.description:
Faridabad, Delhi NCR | On-site | 12-18 years | Reports to the founders Qualification: B. E. / B. Tech - Printing Technology, Polymer or Plastics Engineering, Mechanical, Chemical or Production

Printing is the step that makes our product ours. It's also where most of our quality risk sits, because a defect found at pack is a part we've already paid to mould. 

Your scope is everything that happens to a part after it leaves the tool: UV printing, dye-sublimation, cylindrical and bottle printing, coating, and assembly - through to a finished product ready to pack. 

We have shift managers running the floor, an engineer keeping machines healthy, and a specialist owning colour. What we don't have is anyone accountable for whether our decoration as a whole is good and getting better - or for deciding what we should be able to produce two years from now. 

This role is technical before it is managerial. If you can't stand at a press and tell us why the part in your hand failed, the rest of the job won't work. 

And a large share of the time, the answer isn't the press. Adhesion failures usually trace back to materials - mould release contamination on the part surface, a substrate whose surface energy was never going to accept ink without treatment, plasticiser migrating out of a TPU weeks after it shipped. We want someone who looks upstream before blaming the machine. 

Who owns what - read this

Several roles touch printing, and all of them sit under you: 

- You own the outcome - print and assembly quality, process capability, and what we can and can't produce
 - Operations Managers own daily throughput and dispatch on their shifts
 - The UV Printing Engineer owns machine condition, maintenance and uptime
 - The Colour Management Specialist owns profiles and colour standards

When a defect appears, the diagnosis crosses all four. You decide where it actually came from, what changes, and you're accountable if it comes back. 

What you'd build

- Validated recipes per product and substrate across every process, so output doesn't depend on who's on shift
 - A process capability baseline - what our defect rates actually are, by type and by process. Harder to establish than it sounds, and impossible to improve without
 - A qualification route for new substrates and products, so new product development gets a real answer on printability and assembly rather than an opinion
 - Technology strategy: which process suits which product, where current capability runs out, and what we invest in next
 - A capability roadmap that lets us say yes to work we currently have to decline

Building the team

We're scaling, and most of our operators arrive without print-specific skills. How you build capability matters as much as how you build process. 

- A skill matrix per process - who can set up, who can run, who can judge quality on UV, sublimation, cylindrical and assembly. Certification before anyone operates unsupervised
 - Cross-training as a capacity lever, not an HR nicety. In high-mix production, if one person can set up the bottle line then that line's availability equals their attendance. Depth on every process is how we stop losing days to one person's leave
 - Limit samples, so "acceptable" is a physical object an operator can hold rather than an opinion that shifts by shift. Most quality arguments on a print floor are really definition arguments
 - Train-the-trainer, so capability multiplies rather than routing through you
 - A progression path that gives a good operator a reason to stay beyond the next ₹2, 000 offer
 - The structure of the function itself as we grow - shift coverage, technical specialists, quality

You'd own

- UV flatbed, cylindrical and bottle printing, dye-sublimation, coating and assembly
 - Quality and first-pass yield across the whole post-moulding chain. The number this role is judged on
 - Capacity planning against the production plan
 - Capital decisions for new capacity, and the business cases behind them
 - Customer complaints through to root cause and corrective action
 - The function and its team: shift operations, machine engineering, colour

You need

Real technical depth across our processes. Specifically: 

- Dye-sublimation - transfer printing onto polyester and poly-coated substrates, heat press and 3D vacuum sublimation, and how time, temperature and pressure shift the final result
 - UV inkjet - flatbed printing, LED curing, primer and surface preparation, white ink and varnish layers, and adhesion that holds up weeks later rather than just at inspection
 - Cylindrical and bottle printing - rotary setup, chuck alignment, tapered and non-uniform profiles, maintaining head gap over a curved surface
 - Assembly - multi-part products, fit and tolerance, insert handling, and cosmetic damage prevention on finished parts

Materials - plastics. How substrate behaviour decides what decoration is possible: PC, ABS, PC/ABS, TPU, TPE, PP, PMMA and filled grades. Surface energy and dyne level, and which plastics need corona, plasma or flame treatment before they'll accept anything. Heat deflection limits, which govern what can be sublimated without distorting the part. Mould release carryover, plasticiser migration, and the other upstream causes of a print that fails three weeks later. 

Materials - coatings. Hard coat, soft-touch and PU systems, UV-curable versus two-component thermal cure. Primer and adhesion promoter selection. Mix ratio, pot life and cure schedules for 2K systems. Order of operations - coating over print versus print over coating - and why that choice is rarely reversible. Coating defects: orange peel, fish eyes, pinholes, poor levelling. 

Testing. Cross-hatch adhesion, abrasion, chemical and sweat resistance, and accelerated ageing - enough to establish whether a finish actually holds rather than assuming it will. 

Plus: 

- An engineering degree. B. E. /B. Tech in Printing Technology, Polymer or Plastics Engineering, Mechanical, Chemical or Production. Printing Technology and Polymer Engineering map most closely to this role; a CIPET background is directly relevant on the materials side
 - 12+ years in industrial or digital printing production, with genuine function ownership rather than supervision alone
 - Defect diagnosis you can demonstrate - separating machine, ink, substrate, file, operator and environment as causes rather than guessing
 - Colour management fundamentals, fluent enough to challenge the specialist who owns them
 - Quality improvement with numbers - a defect rate you reduced, and how
 - Equipment selection and commissioning, with capital accountability
 - Demonstrated team building - you've hired, structured and grown a production team, not just inherited one
 - A training system you built, with evidence it worked: skill matrices, certification, limit samples, or whatever you used
 - Leadership across shifts and across technical specialists who know their speciality better than you do
 - Fluent Hindi; working English

Good to have: injection moulding exposure, coating line operation, metals and glass decoration, high-mix short-run environments, screen or pad printing, IMD/IML, drinkware or promotional product decoration. 

Tell us: one print defect you root-caused where the obvious answer turned out to be wrong, one adhesion or coating failure you traced to a material cause, one quality metric you moved with before and after numbers, one operator you developed into something more, and the specific processes, substrates and coatings you've personally run.

Company Description Modutec Ready Panels Pvt Ltd designs and manufactures modular switchboard enclosure systems that simplify panel building for domestic and international markets. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Bengaluru, India, the company focuses on modular technology, standardized components, and flexible configurations to help panel builders streamline fabrication, assembly, and logistics. Its portfolio includes modular LV switchboard enclosures, bayable systems, outdoor and wall-mounted enclosures, and modular accessories. The MODDIS platform supports Form 3 and Form 4 configurations, backed by extensive type testing to IEC 61439 and IEC/TR 61641, with high performance ratings and global-standard protection. Modutec serves customers across Africa, Australia, New Zealand, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East, and offers technical support, training, documentation, and compliance guidance to panel builders, system integrators, consultants, and distribution partners. 

Role Description The Mechanical Design Manager is a full-time, on-site role based in the Greater Bengaluru Area, responsible for leading the mechanical design function for modular switchboard enclosure systems. This role oversees concept development, detailed design, and engineering documentation for enclosure products, ensuring compliance with relevant standards and performance requirements. Day-to-day responsibilities include managing a design team, reviewing and approving CAD models and drawings, coordinating with electrical engineering, production, supply chain, and quality teams, and supporting type testing and product validation activities. The Mechanical Design Manager will optimize designs for manufacturability, flat-pack logistics, and assembly efficiency, while driving continuous improvement in design processes, tools, and standards. The role also involves collaborating with sales and application engineering to provide technical support on enclosure selection, customization, and project-specific solutions. 

Qualifications

- Strong mechanical design and engineering skills, including proficiency in 3D CAD and 2D drafting tools (e. g. , SolidWorks, Inventor, AutoCAD) and familiarity with sheet metal and enclosure design. 
 - Experience with product development for electrical switchboards, enclosures, or industrial equipment, including knowledge of IEC 61439 or similar standards and mechanical performance requirements (IP, IK, short-circuit, internal arc). 
 - Demonstrated ability to lead and mentor design teams, manage workloads and priorities, and collaborate effectively with cross-functional stakeholders in engineering, production, and quality. 
 - Skills in design for manufacturability and assembly, tolerance analysis, material selection (aluminum, steel, copper), and cost optimization. 
 - Competence in documentation and configuration management, including creation and control of BOMs, drawings, specifications, and project reports.

Technical Leader, Cisco Secure Email Threat Defense (ETD) - G11 | Bangalore, India. Your Impact

You will combine deep AI expertise with strong software and security engineering judgment. You will guide the team in selecting the right problems for AI, validating solutions against rigorous quality and safety standards, and operating them effectively at cloud scale. 

- Set the technical strategy and architecture for applied AI in ETD, connecting customer problems and product goals to a clear engineering roadmap.

 - Raise software quality through design and code reviews, automated testing, CI/CD, threat modeling, and engineering practices that improve reliability and delivery speed. 
 - Measure the impact of AI and engineering investments using customer outcomes, telemetry, adoption, quality, and operational metrics; communicate results and trade-offs clearly.

In this role, you will build, train and deploy new LLMs, SLMs, VLMs and AI agents from the ground up - designing architectures, running training experiments, and shipping models into production systems that power the AI assistants of the future. 

We are seeking a high-ownership DevOps & MLOps Engineer with 2-3 years of hands-on experience to own and manage our hybrid cloud infrastructure across Azure (Primary Preference) and AWS (Secondary). In this role, you will be responsible for multi-environment cloud provisioning (Dev, Staging, Production), automated wildcard subdomain routing, API Gateways, centralized logging stacks, database reliability, cloud cost governance, and text-to-speech (TTS) AI pipelines across multiple internal applications. 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Cloud Infrastructure & Automation (IaC)

- Manage secure multi-environment (Dev/Staging/Prod) provisioning on Azure and AWS using Terraform modules. 
 - Standardize container build workflows and infrastructure state management. 2. Networking, Subdomain Routing & Gateways

- Automate wildcard subdomains, CNAME mappings, and ingress routing. 
 - Manage API Gateways (Azure APIM, AWS API Gateway, NGINX, Traefik, Kong). 
 - Handle SSL/TLS lifecycles via Cloudflare, Azure Key Vault, or AWS ACM. 3. AI, Speech & Storage Pipelines

- Maintain low-latency TTS integration pipelines (AWS Polly, Azure Speech Services). 
 - Optimize AWS S3/Azure Blob Storage lifecycle rules, access controls, and CDN delivery. 4. Database Administration & Performance

- Manage, tune, and scale PostgreSQL and Redis databases. 
 - Configure PgBouncer, read-replicas, automated snapshots, and point-in-time recovery. 5. Cost Governance & Observability

- Audit/optimize Azure/AWS spending (Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, rightsizing). 
 - Maintain centralized logging (ELK, Loki, CloudWatch) and metrics dashboards (Prometheus, Grafana). 6. Security, CI/CD & MLOps

- Enforce Zero-Trust IAM, secrets management (Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager), and OAuth/JWT auth. 
 - Manage CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps) for Node. js/Python microservices. 
 - Deploy ML inference endpoints (MLflow, BentoML, SageMaker, Azure ML). 

CANDIDATE REQUIREMENTS

- Experience Level: 2-3 Years
 - Educational Requirement: B. Tech / B. E. / B. S. in Computer Science, IT, or related technical field

Must Have Skills: 

- Experience: 2-3 years of proven hands-on experience in DevOps, Cloud Platform, or Systems Engineering in a fast-paced environment. 
 - Hybrid Cloud: Direct experience managing workloads on AWS (Primary) and exposure to Azure as well. 
 - Infrastructure as Code: High proficiency in writing declarative, modular Terraform code. 
 - Database Management: Practical experience with PostgreSQL and Redis administration, query tuning, and automated backup strategies. 
 - Networking & Gateways: Hands-on setup of API Gateways, wildcard DNS routing, and SSL certificate management. 
 - Audio & Cloud Storage: Experience integrating cloud Speech/TTS APIs (AWS Polly / Azure Speech) and handling cloud object storage (S3 / Azure Blob). 
 - Cost Optimization: Demonstrated track record of auditing and reducing cloud expenditure across AWS or Azure. 
 - Logging & Monitoring: Setup and management of centralized logging (Loki, ELK, or CloudWatch) and metrics collection (Prometheus + Grafana). 
 - Containers & CI/CD: Hands-on expertise with Docker and automated pipeline creation via GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps. 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS (Nice-To-Have)

- Certifications: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104), AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate, or HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate. 
 - MLOps Frameworks: Prior exposure to model deployment frameworks (MLflow, BentoML, TorchServe, Azure ML, or AWS SageMaker). 
 - Backend Debugging: Ability to read and debug Node. js or Python backend code. Please note that we will reach out to ONLY those applicants who satisfy the criteria listed above. 

SALARY DETAILS: commensurate with experience

JOINING DATE: Immediate

JOB TYPE: full time

CONTACT: naveen@hyperworksimaging. com
